scope: Supplement only: Q2 source facts and SFPL/form analysis of visible Q1, Q2 (Q5 optional included). Prior Phase A and Phase B files are unchanged.

primary_sources.ISTQB_CTFL: Official ISTQB CTFL v4.0.1, released 2024-09-15, §5.1.6 printed pp.50-51, https://istqb.org/?download_id=3345&sdm_process_download=1; personally opened and located via PDF text. It states pyramid models differing granularity and test effort allocation; higher layers have lower granularity/isolation and higher execution time; bottom tests are small, isolated, fast, cover small functionality, usually many; top are complex/high-level E2E, slower, cover more functionality, usually few; layer count/names differ. It explicitly gives Cohn 2009's unit/service/UI and another popular model's component, integration(component integration), E2E. This supports B's broad pyramid structure, and shows labels/levels are variable; it does not prescribe an exact share or prove all unit/integration/E2E tests always have those costs.
primary_sources.Mike_Cohn: Mike Cohn, The Forgotten Layer of the Test Automation Pyramid, https://www.mountaingoatsoftware.com/agile/the-forgotten-layer-of-the-test-automation-pyramid; personally opened, page accessible. Text explicitly says unit is pyramid base/largest part; UI top and should be minimized due to brittleness, expense and time; service layer is middle and fills the gap, testing services separately from UI. This directly supports a unit-base/service-middle/UI-top version and rationale. It does not define integration==service in every modern taxonomy or prescribe fixed numeric ratios.

q2_fact_reconciliation.previous: Q2 FACTS was PASS_WITH_NOTES while source statements had not been independently opened.
q2_fact_reconciliation.update: Primary sources now independently substantiate the core model and the caveats: B is a defensible popular modern variant; original Cohn layers are unit/service/UI. FACTS remains PASS_WITH_NOTES, now evidenced. Important nuance: B's shorthand ‘fast’/‘broad E2E’ aligns the general tendency in CTFL/Cohn, but exact speed/cost is contextual; theory itself states this.

Q1.reason: Surface-only wording shows the keyed D is the sole option with professional, calibrated, context-aware phrasing: ‘обоснованный выбор’, ‘по рискам’, ‘ограниченные ресурсы’, ‘цели качества’, ‘полезная обратная связь’. Wrong A asserts ‘без оценки рисков’, ‘автоматически’, ‘оптимальное ... любого продукта’; B says ‘неизменяемое’, ‘один раз’, ‘исключить пересмотр ... даже при изменении’; C says ‘только’ past reporting and excludes future decisions. These extreme claims are conspicuous and invite elimination without knowing testing theory. Yet D's domain terms themselves can signal expertise, so the cue's actual impact for a reasonably trained reader cannot be inferred from wording alone. No formal style-only proof that D is guessable; cannot mark PASS based only on similar length or complete structure. No independent responder study was run.

Q2.reason: B's surface phrasing is balanced/qualified (‘конкретное распределение выбирают по рискам и стоимости обратной связи’). A uses ‘обязательные проценты, не меняющиеся’, D ‘всегда ... независимо от рисков’, both self-discrediting absolutes. C is also overconfident (‘нужно’) and states a visibly reversed order plus ‘большинства ветвей ... на широком пользовательском пути’; even without knowing the canonical pyramid, that pairing can sound like overuse of a broad method, although identifying the reversal needs domain knowledge. This yields a nontrivial key-tone cue: the lone moderate caveated answer contrasts with two absolute wrong options. Conversely C is nearly the same length as B (175 vs 176 chars), has a full parallel structure and plausible professional vocabulary; length does not isolate B. Overall whether tone alone enables a competent non-specialist to pick B remains uncertain; balanced wording is also substantively appropriate. No user study; no claim of automatic SFPL failure.

Q5_optional.reason: A is similarly calibrated and detailed, but B/C/D all offer specific definitions and contents; all three use ‘только’/exclude key rationale, creating a shared rather than unique signal. A/B lengths are 158/159 characters and the wrong answers are structurally complete. These visible signals do not uniquely reveal A, though practical guessing remains unmeasured.

cross_question_conclusion.reason: Q1 and Q2 both show a repeated correct-option register of contextual, risk-aware qualification against wrong-option absolutes, strongest in Q1 and Q2 A/D. Q2 C adds a domain-plausible but wrong reversed pyramid. This is a concrete style/modality concern independent of answer truth, not an automatic FAIL: absolutism is semantically germane to the false claims, while calibrated language naturally fits the correct principles. Equal/near-equal lengths do not settle perceived plausibility. A non-domain cue assessment needs blind readers explicitly instructed to judge tone/form without solving content; none was conducted.

limitations: Source review covered only the requested CTFL §5.1.6 and Cohn article, not every claim in Q2 theory or the complete MCQ file.
The SFPL judgment is qualitative inspection of visible text; actual guessability by a non-expert is empirical and remains unmeasured.
No original Phase A/B output was edited.
